interactions.summary: Jiang presses the class on whether a spirit can perceive time and space, and a student answers that without a body the soul is no longer subject to those conditions.

Jiang builds the metaphysical model: body-based sensation makes both distance and temporal sequence possible, so paradise as spirit world lies beyond time and space, with everything existing at once and forever.

A student asks how Greek spirits can appear or act if they are bodiless, and Jiang answers that they do so by taking possession of animals or people, thereby borrowing a body's access to time and space.

speaker_notes.note: The first student segment is transcript-noisy and appears to capture overlapping voices before the more coherent answer arrives in seg-0155.

claims.claim: Jiang says body-based sensation is what makes both distance and temporal sequence intelligible, so without a body one cannot properly experience time or space.
Jiang invokes Kant to define space as sensation mediated by the senses and time as the felt sequence of cause and effect.
Jiang says paradise is a universe where time and space do not exist, so everything exists at once and forever and multiple symbolic universes can coexist simultaneously.
Jiang says Greek spirits act within the material world by possessing animals or people, because only through a body can they receive time and space.

signature_moments.moment: Without a body you would have no conception of distance, because space itself is a product of sensation.
signature_moments.source_phrase: if you didn't have a body, you wouldn't have a conception of distance
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's clearest compression of why paradise must be narrated differently from ordinary earthly reality.

signature_moments.moment: Paradise becomes a universe where everything exists at once and forever.
signature_moments.source_phrase: everything exists at once and forever
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's most reusable metaphysical formulation and explains why parallel symbolic worlds can coexist in Jiang's reading.

signature_moments.moment: A spirit can enter time and space only by taking possession of somebody's body.
signature_moments.source_phrase: only if they can take possession of someone's body
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This preserves Jiang's bridge between disembodied paradise and mythic intervention in the human world.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang defines time as sequence and cause-and-effect generated through bodily sensation.
Jiang defines space as sensation made possible through the five senses and bodily existence.
The mechanism by which Greek spirits borrow a material body and thereby enter the conditions of time and space.

chronology_notes.note: This packet develops the parallel-universe claim from packet 0019 into a more explicit body/time/space model, then uses Greek possession to explain how a spirit world can still touch embodied history.

uncertainty_notes.note: The opening discussion is transcript-fragmentary, so the strongest anchor for the packet is Jiang's clearer formulation in seg-0156 plus the possession example in seg-0159.
